question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹1,200 at an interest rate of 4% per month for 5 months.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total percentage interest = **Interest Rate** × **Time**

Net interest rate = 4% × 5 = 20%

**Simple Interest** = 20% of ₹1,200

SI = 0.2 × 1200 = ₹240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal** (P) = ₹1,200

**Rate** (R) = 4% per month

**Time** (T) = 5 months

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/453d595fa6e7c703b36309838f083234a03410869162056052549b42f28f0e69.png] 

Using the formula for **Simple Interest**:

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (1200 × 4 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 1200 × 20 ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 12 × 20

⇒ SI = 240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total **Amount** (A) is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Simple Interest**: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Unit Consistency

Always ensure that the **Interest Rate** and **Time** are in the same units (e.g., both monthly or both yearly) before calculation.

Annual Rate Conversion

To convert a monthly rate to an **Annual Rate**, multiply by 12. For example, 4% per month is equivalent to 48% per annum.
